clinician.final_diagnosis: Idiopathic form of acro-osteolysis involving the distal phalanges
clinician.trajectory_summary: A female market worker in her 50s presented with 6 months of fingertip pain and swelling. Physical examination revealed mild clubbing of thumbs and index fingers without nail deformities. Radiography and MRI identified band acro-osteolysis of the distal phalanges of both thumbs and index fingers, and a destructive change in the DIP joint of the right middle finger. Laboratory investigations including inflammatory markers (CRP), serum alkaline phosphatase, calcium, intact parathyroid hormone, rheumatoid factor, anti-DNA antibodies, anti-Scl-70 antibody, and anticentromere antibodies were normal or negative, excluding systemic inflammatory or autoimmune etiologies. No history or clinical evidence supported alternative causes such as Raynaud's, psoriasis, trauma, frostbite, or exposure to PVC. No clinical course or treatment response was documented.
